correctness.rationale: On the orthogonal complement of the constants, the averaged cosine and sine Rayleigh quotients at frequencies 1 and 2 are (pB+4A)/(2n) and qB/(2n). Substituting A=(1-B)/t gives the two affine bounds. They cross at B=4/(4+t(q-p)); the slope of the first-harmonic bound changes sign at t=4/p, yielding exactly the stated maximizing budgets, including B in [p/q,1] at equality. Class-constant rates attain the bound: the smallest nonzero even mode is qb and the smallest odd mode is pb+2a. The first-harmonic bound is tight at every optimum, so both cosine and sine are gap eigenvectors. The tangent component of their common equation forces sin(pi/n)(w[j-1]-w[j])=0 at each vertex, and the radial equation then forces equal rung rates. This also applies to n=3 and to zero rungs. The fixed-price large-n claims follow from n²p→π² and n²q→4π². VERIFICATION.md and check_mobius.py were inspected; the script was not executed. Its finite numerical trials supplement but do not certify equality-case rigidity.
residual_risks: No formal verification or fresh numerical replay is claimed.
